title: Auto Loan Calculator
description: Calculate your monthly car payment including sales tax, trade-in value, and down payment.

formula.summary: The loan amount is the vehicle price plus sales tax, minus the down payment and trade-in value, then amortized like any standard installment loan.
formula.expression: Loan = Price + Tax − Down − TradeIn, then M = Loan × [r(1+r)^n] / [(1+r)^n − 1]

variables.meaning: Sales tax on the taxable amount (price minus trade-in, in most states)

examples.title: $32,000 car, $4,000 down, no trade-in, 6.5% tax, 60 months at 7%

faqs.question: How does a trade-in reduce my taxes?
faqs.answer: In most U.S. states, sales tax is charged only on the price minus your trade-in value, so a trade-in reduces both your loan amount and the tax you owe - a meaningful double benefit.

faqs.question: Does this include fees like title and registration?
faqs.answer: No - this calculator focuses on price, tax, down payment, trade-in, and financing. Add any dealer fees or registration costs to the vehicle price for a more complete picture.

seoContent.heading: How auto loan amounts are calculated
seoContent.body: Unlike a simple personal loan, an auto loan usually needs to account for sales tax, which is charged as part of the purchase and often rolled into the amount financed. This calculator applies your state's tax rate to the taxable amount, adds it to the vehicle price, then subtracts your down payment and trade-in value to arrive at the actual loan principal.

seoContent.heading: Choosing a loan term
seoContent.body: Longer terms (72 months or more) lower the monthly payment but increase total interest paid and raise the risk of being 'upside down' - owing more than the car is worth - for longer, since cars depreciate faster than a long loan pays down principal. A shorter term keeps total interest lower and builds equity faster.
